title: A section of a split unipotent torsor over an affine scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $U$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $U$ has a finite split series $U=U_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq U_m=1$ of smooth connected closed subgroup schemes, each normal in its predecessor, with each represented fppf quotient $U_j/U_{j+1}$ isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{a,k}$ [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors, def-sc-gm-ga]. Here $m=0$ is allowed. Let $S$ be an affine $k$-scheme of finite type, and let $p:P\to S$ be a represented right $U$-torsor [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors]: $p$ is flat, surjective and finitely presented, with a right action for which $(x,u)\mapsto(x,xu)$ is an isomorphism $P\times_kU\simeq P\times_SP$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then there exists a section $s:S\to P$ with $p\circ s=\operatorname{id}_S$. Neither $k$ nor $S$ is required to be perfect or reduced, respectively; no commutativity or centrality hypothesis is imposed on $U$.

source.place: Proposition 16.55(b), printed p.344; split series convention in Definition 6.33 and Section 14.61, with additive affine torsors in Example 2.72, printed p.61.

proof.text: Proceed by induction on the length m of the displayed split series. If m=0, then U=1. The torsor comparison in the hypothesis is the diagonal P\simeq P\times_S P, so p is a monomorphism. It is flat and locally of finite presentation by the torsor hypotheses, hence an open immersion by [lem-pe-flat-lfp-monomorphism-open]. Since it is also surjective, this open immersion is an isomorphism, and its inverse is the required section.

source.place: Proposition 16.55(b), printed p.344, with the length-zero case written out using the flat-monomorphism criterion

proof.text: Assume m>0 and put N=U_1. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] to the closed normal subgroup N of U. It supplies the affine finite-type quotient Q=U/N, a faithfully flat finitely presented quotient map q with scheme-theoretic kernel N, and the represented fppf quotient; the given split-series clause identifies Q with \mathbf G_{a,k}. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-extension-torsor-reduction] to q and the represented U-torsor P\to S. We obtain a represented right Q-torsor R=P/N\to S, and for any section a:S\to R the pullback P_a=P\times_{R,a}S is a represented right N-torsor whose section composes to a section of P.

source.place: Proposition 16.55(b), printed p.344; quotient and torsor reduction as in Example 2.68 and Proposition 2.69, printed p.60

proof.text: Write the affine base as S=Spec A. Transport the Q-torsor R along its given isomorphism Q\simeq\mathbf G_{a,k}; its flat, surjective, finitely presented map and torsor comparison are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-additive-affine-torsor-section], so R has a section a. The tail N=U_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq U_m=1 is a split series of length m-1 with the same smoothness, connectedness and finite-type hypotheses. The induction hypothesis applied to the N-torsor P_a therefore gives a section b:S\to P_a. The final clause of [lem-sfb-normal-extension-torsor-reduction] composes b with P_a\to P to obtain e:S\to P and p\circ e=id_S, completing the induction.

source.place: Example 2.72, printed p.61, and Proposition 16.55(b), printed p.344
